facts.content: 4-day history of very itchy, sore, red rash.

facts.content: Rash is located on the chest, hands, and inside elbows, and not on the face.
facts.source_text: Location: chest, hands, inside elbows; no face

facts.content: Severe pruritus is causing disturbed sleep, impaired focus at work, and limits hiking.
facts.source_text: Severity/impact: severe pruritus; sleep disturbed; impaired focus at work; limits hiking

facts.content: Skin is dry with some cracked areas, but there is no bleeding or discharge.
facts.source_text: Skin: dry; some cracked areas; no bleeding or discharge

facts.content: No fever or elevated temperature.
Bowels are normal.
No cough or shortness of breath.
Urine is normal.

Patient tried OTC steroid cream with no relief.
Patient tried antihistamines with no relief.
Patient has no known allergies.

facts.source_text: 31 y/o; lives with flatmates; project manager at pharmaceutical company

facts.content: Patient is a nonsmoker and drinks a few beers per week.

facts.source_text: Pruritic erythematous rash — likely eczema flare (itchy, dry/cracked skin; distribution incl. antecubital fossae; prior eczema; no systemic sx)

facts.content: Sleep disturbance secondary to pruritus.

facts.source_text: Rx: stronger topical steroid (name/strength not specified)

facts.content: Use emollients during bath/shower regularly for 7-10 days.
facts.source_text: Emollients for bath/shower; regular use for 7–10 days

facts.content: Antihistamine trial suggested; consider fexofenadine as a stronger option.
facts.source_text: Antihistamine trial; consider fexofenadine as stronger option

facts.content: Keep a trigger diary for clothing, soaps/shower gels, and other exposures.
facts.source_text: Keep trigger diary (clothing, soaps/shower gels, other exposures)
